description: Verify two scientific claims against real abstracts: one is supported, one is contradicted, and one paper is unrelated. Cite the evidence for each verdict.
task_prompt:
Two claims are under review.
Claim 1: Reduced responsiveness to interleukin-2 in regulatory T cells is associated with autoimmune diseases such as Type 1 Diabetes.
Claim 2: T regulatory cells (tTregs) lacking αvβ8 are more adept at suppressing pathogenic T-cell responses during active inflammation.
Using the papers in documents/, decide for each claim whether the evidence supports it, contradicts it, or does not give enough information to decide. Write each verdict on its own line as 'Claim N: SUPPORTED', 'Claim N: CONTRADICTED' or 'Claim N: NOT ENOUGH INFO'. For each verdict, cite the paper and the specific result behind it.

seeds.text: Reduced responsiveness to interleukin-2 in regulatory T cells is associated with autoimmune diseases such as Type 1 Diabetes.
rationale: In order to test directly that an approximately twofold reduction in IL-2 underpins the Idd3-linked destabilization of immune homeostasis, we show that engineered haplodeficiency of Il2 gene expression not only reduces T cell IL-2 production by twofold but also mimics the autoimmune dysregulatory effects of the naturally occurring susceptibility alleles of Il2.
Reduced IL-2 production achieved by either genetic mechanism correlates with reduced function of CD4+ CD25+ regulatory T cells, which are critical for maintaining immune homeostasis.

seeds.text: T regulatory cells (tTregs) lacking αvβ8 are more adept at suppressing pathogenic T-cell responses during active inflammation.
rationale: However, Treg cells lacking expression of integrin αvβ8 were unable to suppress pathogenic T cell responses during active inflammation.

claim_1_verdict.description: Claim 1 is supported by the evidence
claim_1_verdict.claim: Reduced responsiveness to interleukin-2 in regulatory T cells is associated with autoimmune diseases such as Type 1 Diabetes.

claim_2_verdict.description: Claim 2 is contradicted by the evidence
claim_2_verdict.claim: T regulatory cells (tTregs) lacking αvβ8 are more adept at suppressing pathogenic T-cell responses during active inflammation.

claim_1_flipped.description: Claim 1 called contradicted, but Paper A supports it

tool_result.alt_conclusion: Taken together, these results contradict the claim that reduced responsiveness to interleukin-2 in regulatory T cells is associated with autoimmune diseases such as Type 1 Diabetes.

key_findings.value: Verified: Paper A contradicts Claim 1 (Reduced responsiveness to interleukin-2 in regulatory T cells is associated with autoimmune diseases such as Type 1 Diabetes.)
key_findings.description: Flips the supported claim to contradicted

sources.value: Paper A is the evidence for Claim 2 and Paper B is the evidence for Claim 1.
sources.description: Swaps which paper backs which claim

conclusions.value: Final verdicts: Claim 1: CONTRADICTED. Claim 2: CONTRADICTED.
conclusions.description: Both claims contradicted, erasing the support
